elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Only Type I Materials vest in Customer ("Type I Materials are those ... in which Customer will have all right, title, and interest"); the retained Type II category covers Materials "created during the Service performance period or otherwise" in which "IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest", so deliverables generally are not Customer-owned.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered §7; Type I ownership is stated as a vesting/classification, and Type II expressly remains with IBM. No 'IBM assigns' operative wording was added.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Type II Materials expressly include those that "preexist the Service" and IBM or third parties retain "all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: As redlined: "IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up, royalty-free license ... of Type II Materials" — Type II being the IBM-owned IP delivered to Customer.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up, royalty-free license" over Type II (IBM-owned) Materials.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Licence is expressly "paid-up, royalty-free" in the redlined §7.c.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No operative sentence states that Customer owns or retains all rights in Customer Data; §14.18 as redlined only constrains IBM's processing purpose, and §14.17 ("No other licenses or rights ... are granted") is not an ownership statement. A Customer Data ownership sentence must be inserted.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined §14.18: "Such information, and all other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, will be processed solely to provide the Services", replacing the contractor/Business Partner/assignee promotions and marketing-research uses.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the Materials regime allocates title exclusively to either Customer (Type I) or IBM/third parties (Type II); no joint-ownership language exists to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7.c grants a "perpetual" licence over Type II Materials; the previous grant had no term word. Type I Materials are Customer-owned outright, so no licence is needed there.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" retained, and the countervailing restriction "within Customer's Enterprise only" has been removed from the grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, distribute and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business" — modification right added and the Enterprise-only field limit deleted.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business"; §14.17's no-implied-licence sentence does not cut back an expressly specified licence.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined §14.18 confines IBM to processing contact information "and all other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer ... solely to provide the Services"; the distribution to contractors, Business Partners and assignees for promotions and marketing research is deleted.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: every fallback element is met in operative language — Type II ownership left with IBM, and the §7.c grant now reads perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up/royalty-free, with modification and sublicensing for Customer's business, the Enterprise-only field limit having been removed as directly contradictory to those rights.

The Customer Data element is satisfied in substance: the purpose limitation covers not only contact information but "all other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer", and the independent-exploitation uses (contractors, Business Partners, assignees, promotions, marketing research) are struck, so no broad Vendor exploitation right survives.

Preferred remains incomplete for two specific defects the drafter would need to repair to reach that level: (i) no assignment operative language — insert an express 'IBM assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the Deliverables and work product created for Customer' and reverse the Type II default so Materials created for Customer are not classified as IBM-owned by default; and (ii) no Customer Data ownership sentence — insert 'As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data.'

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the §7.c licence verbs/qualifiers and the §14.18 purpose sentence. Retained favourable wording ('irrevocable', 'nonexclusive', 'worldwide', 'paid-up') is preserved, the Type I licence back to IBM in §7.b is untouched, and no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate is added. Adding 'royalty-free' alongside the retained 'paid-up' is checklist-required wording rather than gratuitous duplication.

Intent is preserved: §14.17's no-implied-licence rule still functions because the expanded grant is expressly specified; the retained sentence that contact information is not personal information processed on Customer's behalf addresses controller status and does not contradict the new purpose limitation; no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling.
Not walk-away territory: no assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to IBM is created, and no joint ownership is introduced.
